4A)   A specimen of steel 20 mm diameter with a gauge length of 200 mm is tested to  
  destruction. It has an extension of 0.25 mm under a load of 80 kN and the load at elastic  
  limit is 102 kN. The ultimate load is 130 kN.  
  The total extension at fracture is 56 mm and diameter at neck is 15 mm. Find              (5)  
  (i) The stress at elastic limit. (ii) Young's modulus. (iii) Percentage elongation. (iv)  
  Percentage reduction in area. (v) Ultimate tensile stress.  
  
4B)   A circular rod of 25 mm diameter and 500 mm long is subjected to a tensile force of 60  
  kN. Determine modulus of rigidity, bulk modulus and change in volume if Poisson's         (3)  
  $$ratio = 0.3 and Young's modulus E = 2 \times  105 N/mm2$$

5B)             A compound bar of length 600 mm consists of a strip of aluminium 40 mm wide and 20  
  mm thick and a strip of steel 60 mm wide × 15 mm thick rigidly joined at the ends. If  
  elastic modulus of aluminium and steel are 1 × 105 N/mm2 and 2 × 105 N/mm2,           (5)  
  determine the stresses developed in each material and the extension of the compound  
  bar when axial tensile force of 60 kN acts.
